reason: The passage illustrates David demonstrating responsibility and accountability for the people's welfare. When Saul and Israel are paralyzed by fear of Goliath, David steps forward with the words 'your servant will go and fight with this Philistine' (עַבְדְּךָ֣ יֵלֵ֔ךְ וְנִלְחַ֖ם עִם־ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֥י). He takes personal responsibility for removing the threat to the nation, trusting in God's aid. His willingness to bear risk on behalf of the people, his successful defense of them against their enemy, and the narrative's implicit approval of his actions all suggest that the text presents such personal accountability for the people's welfare as exemplary leadership behavior.
